subject: Demo follow-up: environment preflight and hosted quickstart
thread_body:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 May 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Demo follow-up: environment preflight and hosted quickstart

Samir —

Thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap from the demo and a few requests so we can validate the best deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private) for NimbusRetail. High-level notes:

- You liked the latency profile on the 16k-context model we showed and the realtime batching demo.
- Your primary concerns are data residency, predictable throughput for peak shopping windows, and SSO/integration with your IdP.

To help us recommend the right initial setup, could you confirm the following items?
1) Traffic profile: average qps and expected peak qps (5-min window), plus burst behavior (how long bursts last).
2) Latency SLO target (p50/p95) for interactive experiences.
3) Data handling: do you need zero-retention (no-store) and/or logs disabled for PII? Any specific region requirement (e.g., us-west-2)?
4) Auth: SAML/OKTA requirement for service-to-service? API key rotation cadence?
5) Timeline: when do you want to begin functional testing (sandbox) and pilot traffic?

Recommended first pass (based on our conversation): start on Hosted API (fastest onboarding + staging endpoints) with a pathway to Reserved Dedicated for predictable peak capacity. Private/VPC would be recommended only if legal/regulatory audits require customer-managed infrastructure.

Next steps I propose:
- We provision a short-lived staging endpoint (no prod keys) for you to run the test set.
- Grace will confirm default rate limits and burst allowances and share a preflight checklist.
- If staging looks good, we draft a minimal mutual action plan and discuss reserved capacity sizing.

Can you share the traffic numbers above and any internal security docs we should pre-check? I attached a short hosted preflight checklist and the quickstart playbook for your engineers.

If it helps, I'm available Thursday 9am or Friday 1pm PT for a technical handoff — otherwise tell me a time that works.

Cheers,
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

----

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@nimbusretail.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 May 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: environment preflight and hosted quickstart

Thanks Avery — great session. A few quick answers and follow-up questions:

- Traffic: expected steady-state ~2–3 TPS (requests per second) for personalization calls; peak up to ~15 TPS during flash sales, bursts usually last ~3–10 minutes.
- Latency: we shoot for p95 < 400ms for the personalization endpoint; p50 ideally under 120ms.
- Data: we cannot send raw customer PII to vendors by default; we prefer a no-store option for anything that contains email/phone. Region: us-west-2 preferred.
- Auth: we use Okta and will need SAML for console access; API calls can use rotating API tokens.
- Timeline: we'd like a staging endpoint within 10 business days if possible; pilot in ~4–6 weeks.

Questions: what are Redwood's default per-endpoint rate limits for hosted eval endpoints? Is there short-term burst allowance above the steady limit? Also curious on pricing delta between hosted pilot (metered) vs a small Dedicated pool — ballpark numbers would help our procurement team.

I've attached our internal security overview and SSO requirements (PDF). Happy to jump on a follow-up call with your solutions engineer.

—Samir
CTO, NimbusRetail

----

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Wed, 09 May 2028 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Demo follow-up: environment preflight and hosted quickstart

Grace / Rishi — forwarding Samir's answers. Can you confirm the hosted defaults we quoted during the call and whether we can meet the p95 400ms goal with the model family they saw? Also please confirm how quickly we can stand up a staging endpoint in us-west-2 with no-store enabled and SAML console provisioning.

Attachments: Samir_SecurityOverview.pdf (attached by prospect).

Thanks — aiming to get this back to them before EOD so they can hit the 10-business-day window.

Avery

----

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: environment preflight and hosted quickstart

Hi Avery / Samir —

Thanks for the details, Samir — that helps a lot. Short answers up front, then a few implementation notes:

1) Default hosted evaluation limits (current standard):
   - Per-endpoint steady concurrency: 60 requests/sec (rps) per endpoint.
   - Short burst allowance: up to 300 rps for 30–120s windows for warm-up/bursts (subject to fair-use checks).
   - Token throughput budgets are enforced at account-level; for interactive text gen we typically recommend planning for ~250k tokens/min for pilot traffic — we can increase temporarily for flash-sale windows.

2) Latency and model choice: the 16k-context model shown in the demo is expected to meet p95 < 400ms for short prompts in us-west-2 under the traffic profile you described if we enable continuous batching and warm cache. Rishi — we should call out that longer context or heavy system prompts will increase p95.

3) Data residency / retention: Hosted can pin storage to us-west-2 and we support a no-store mode for request payloads (enterprise setting) that prevents request/response retention in logs. For customers requiring provable isolation and customer-managed keys we recommend Private (VPC) or Dedicated with ZK-keying options.

4) Auth / SSO: we can provision SAML SSO for the console and use rotating API keys for programmatic access. Okta integration is supported; SSO onboarding usually takes 2–3 business days once we have IdP metadata.

5) Timeline & staging: we can provision a staging endpoint in us-west-2 with no-store enabled within 48 business hours after we receive the signed sandbox NDA and the short preflight checklist (attached). For early validation we will issue scoped API credentials with limited token budgets.

6) Pricing note: hosted pilot is metered and generally lower up-front OPEX; small Dedicated pools have a monthly committed cost but give predictable throughput and slightly lower per-token unit costs at scale. I can provide rough numbers to procurement if you share expected monthly token volumes.

Attachments: included a curated hosted preflight checklist and quickstart playbook (links/attachments).

Proposed next step: Samir — if you confirm the staging window and send the signed sandbox NDA, we'll kick off provisioning and schedule a 60-minute handoff with our solutions engineer and your infra lead.

Happy to jump on the call to walk through the preflight items.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

"Attachments: nimbus-hosted-checklist.pdf (sent by prospect), redwood-quickstart-playbook.md (sent by Redwood)"
